newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil firms despite physical.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil firms despite physical.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps firmed late afternoon Wednesday on technicals despite agressive physical offers in the face of prompt oversupply, brokers said.
"The swaps are firming because of some paper play despite the low physical offers," one trader said.
Fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $98.50/$100.00 per tonne up from Tuesday's $98.00/$99.25 and this morning's $97.50/$99.25, brokers said.
Brokers said the market had picked up due to crack and East-West spread plays by some paper players.
They said second-half February traded earlier in the day at $100.25 and $100.50 per tonne.
Others said the swap also picked up on market perception that the physical market was over sold.
On Tuesday, one major offered a 20,000-tonne cargo to a low $95.00 per tonne, down $2.00 from Monday.
The gas oil swaps recovered most of its early day losses and was last quoted $25.25/$25.35 per barrel.
Traders said the market was drifting sideways in quiet trading at midday on Wednesday as the market wound down for the Lunar New Year and the Eid-el-Fitri holidays, traders said.

Jet fuel was steady at the higher levels reflecting the tight prompt supplies and strong regional buying interest. The February jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was last quoted $4.40/$4.80 per barrel.

On the physical market premiums remain strong with a cargo sold on Monday to China at $2.05 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, up 20 cents from the previous traded level.
